terms.translation: A charge an agreement says may apply if it ends before the agreed date.
terms.analogy: A service plan lists a charge for cancelling before month twelve.

terms.translation: A form giving permission to share specified records with a named recipient.
terms.analogy: A clinic form identifies which records may be sent to a specialist.

terms.translation: The part of an agreement that explains when and how payment is due.
terms.analogy: An invoice says payment is due within 30 days.

terms.translation: A section explaining which information must be kept private and under what conditions.
terms.analogy: A workplace agreement identifies which internal documents must stay private.

terms.translation: A list of proposed procedures with a separate estimated price for each one.
terms.analogy: An estimate lists the exam, X-rays, and cleaning as separate items.

terms.translation: A policy describing how long different records are kept and what happens afterward.
terms.analogy: A business keeps invoices for the period listed in its policy.

terms.translation: A record of a rental home’s condition at the start of a tenancy.
terms.analogy: The tenant and landlord write down an existing scratch on a door.

terms.translation: Pay before deductions such as taxes or employee contributions.
terms.analogy: A payslip lists gross pay and the amount deposited after deductions.

terms.translation: An app setting that controls whether and when the app can access your location.
terms.analogy: A maps app asks to see your location only while you use it.

terms.translation: A written change to part of an existing agreement.
terms.analogy: Both parties sign a page that changes the delivery date.

terms.translation: Charges for services such as water, electricity, or gas.
terms.analogy: A rental agreement says which bills are included in the rent.

terms.translation: Money paid back for an expense someone already covered.
terms.analogy: An employee submits a receipt for an approved work trip.

terms.translation: A clause that can make each person named on the lease responsible for the full amount owed, depending on its terms.
terms.analogy: One roommate moves out early. The landlord asks the other roommate for the full rent under this clause.

terms.translation: The total earnings counted from the start of the year through the current pay period.
terms.analogy: My October payslip shows what I earned since January next to what I earned this month.

terms.translation: When an organization sends information about you to another organization or service.
terms.analogy: A booking app sends a name and reservation number to the company operating the venue.

terms.translation: The part of a project agreement that lists the work and deliverables the price covers.
terms.analogy: My quote includes a logo and two revisions. A social media kit would need its own line.

terms.translation: A list of items in a rental and the condition they are in at handover.
terms.analogy: I noted that the oven light was already broken before I moved my boxes in.

terms.translation: The date range covered by a particular payslip.
terms.analogy: My deposit came in on Friday, but the slip covers the two weeks ending the Sunday before.

terms.translation: Small browser files used to track how people use a website.
terms.analogy: A shop counts how many visitors reach checkout and where people leave the site.

terms.translation: The smallest quantity a supplier agrees to sell in one order.
terms.analogy: The supplier quotes a price per mug, with a minimum order of 24 mugs.

terms.translation: A school or clinic form that records which people have permission to pick up a child.
terms.analogy: A parent adds a grandparent to the school list before going on a work trip.

terms.translation: An offer that depends on one or more listed requirements being met.
terms.analogy: An offer letter says the employer is waiting for two references before confirming the appointment.

terms.translation: A document that reduces the amount owed on an invoice or records credit on an account.
terms.analogy: A supplier sends a credit note after two damaged items are returned.

terms.translation: A date when the rent can be reviewed under the agreement.
terms.analogy: The lease lists July as the first date for a review and explains how the tenant will be told.

terms.translation: Permission for a healthcare provider to send referral details to another provider involved in your care.
terms.analogy: My clinic asks which report can be shared with the physiotherapy office.

terms.translation: The amount the policyholder may have to pay toward a covered claim before the insurer pays its share.
terms.analogy: The policy lists a deductible for accidental damage, so the policyholder pays that portion of the repair bill.

terms.translation: A buyer's written order identifying what it wants to buy and the terms it is requesting.
terms.analogy: The shop sends a numbered order showing 30 chairs and the agreed delivery address.

terms.translation: A document that explains what an organization collects, why it uses it, and who may receive it.
terms.analogy: A newsletter explains which data it saves when you sign up and how you can request its removal.

terms.translation: A record of what a utility meter displayed when a new tenancy started.
terms.analogy: I photographed the electricity meter on key collection day so I had the starting number.

terms.translation: A period during notice when an employee stays employed but is asked to stop doing some or all of their usual work.
terms.analogy: An employee stops working with clients while waiting for their listed end date.

terms.translation: A written estimate for proposed treatment that can help you compare expected charges before deciding.
terms.analogy: A clinic lists the expected price of a crown and separates the lab fee from the appointment fee.

terms.translation: The invoice date records when the bill was issued. The due date tells you when payment is expected.
terms.analogy: An invoice is issued on March 3 and lists April 2 as the payment deadline.

terms.translation: A lease term about a tenant's ability to use their home without unreasonable interference.
terms.analogy: The lease explains how visits for inspections are arranged while the tenant is living there.

terms.translation: A request asking an organization for access to the personal information it holds about you.
terms.analogy: A former customer asks a subscription service for a copy of the information on their account.

terms.translation: The amount left after payroll deductions, usually the amount paid to you.
terms.analogy: I compare the net pay line on the slip with the deposit in my bank app.

terms.translation: The part of an employment agreement that states expected working hours and may describe how scheduling changes are handled.
terms.analogy: An offer lists 40 hours per week and says where to check the shift schedule.

terms.translation: A lease provision that describes when and how a party can end a fixed term early.
terms.analogy: The lease says the tenant can give written notice after month six if the listed conditions are met.

terms.translation: A sign-in check that uses two different types of evidence to confirm the account holder.
terms.analogy: I enter my password and approve the sign-in in a separate authenticator app.

terms.translation: Records that help show what a financial entry or claim refers to.
terms.analogy: A shop keeps the supplier invoice and proof of payment together for one purchase.

terms.translation: Standards or checks used to decide whether a delivery meets the agreed requirements.
terms.analogy: A website project says the contact form must send a test message before handover is approved.

terms.translation: The point when access keys are given to or returned by the tenant, sometimes recorded in writing.
terms.analogy: I signed for two door keys and a building tag when I moved in.

terms.translation: The number or type of changes included in a project quote.
terms.analogy: Two rounds of edits are included. A third round is quoted as extra work.

terms.translation: A line showing pay recorded for overtime in that pay period, where the employer lists it separately.
terms.analogy: I compared the overtime hours on my slip with the extra Saturday shift on my timesheet.

terms.translation: Permission to send promotional communications that can be offered separately from some account settings.
terms.analogy: I made an account and left the newsletter checkbox empty.

terms.translation: The range of dates a seller expects an order to arrive.
terms.analogy: The supplier gave me Tuesday through Thursday as the expected arrival window.

terms.translation: The maximum amount the policy says it will pay for a specified type of claim or benefit.
terms.analogy: An insurance summary lists a separate limit for luggage claims.

terms.translation: A clause saying which document takes priority if parts of an agreement conflict.
terms.analogy: The signed order form and the supplier terms give different dates, so I check which one takes priority.

terms.translation: Someone an organization may contact in an urgent situation, as described on the form.
terms.analogy: I listed my sister as the contact to call if the clinic needs to reach someone quickly.

terms.translation: The process of checking and confirming the hours someone recorded for work.
terms.analogy: My supervisor approves Monday's timesheet before payroll processes it.

terms.translation: A request asking an organization to fix inaccurate information it holds about you.
terms.analogy: I ask the service to update a surname it spelled incorrectly on my account.

terms.translation: A number or short label used to match a bill with the related order or payment.
terms.analogy: I put the invoice number in the payment reference so the supplier can match the transfer.

terms.translation: A set of building rules covering common spaces used by multiple residents.
terms.analogy: The building rules say where bicycles can be stored and when the laundry room closes.

terms.translation: A form that asks whether a school can take or use a student's photo for listed purposes.
terms.analogy: A family agrees to a class photo kept inside the school and declines use on social media.

terms.translation: A document that records when someone can resume working and may describe any restrictions.
terms.analogy: The note says the person can return Monday with a temporary lifting restriction.
